..A concerning situation continue to evolve across 
Arizona through Thursday evening, with threats of flooding/flash 
flooding, severe thunderstorms, and tornadoes. A strong low 
pressure system sliding south-southeastward along the coast of
California. This pushing a deep moisture surge, with tropical and
subtropical origins, and providing an environment favorable for 
severe weather. The low will eventually lifts through the Great 
Basin on Thursday, shifting the area of heavy weather and strong
to severe thunderstorms more eastward, across eastern AZ, 
dragging a cold front through the region late Thursday into 
Friday.

It as already been an active morning with severe thunderstorm and
tornado warnings as mesoanalysis showed a 50-55kt jet overhead at
500mb, as well as a strengthening southeasterly low-level jet 
advecting warm air and high dewpoints into northern AZ with MLCAPE
values around 250-500 J/kg across most of the region. This 
transport of warm air and high dewpoints is continuing and MLCAPE 
is now around 500 with pockets of 1000 J/kg across the region. 
This is still coupled with bulk shear around 50kts and 1km storm 
relative helicity 100-250 m2/s2, we are still seeing scattered 
discrete supercell thunderstorms initiating along and north of the
higher terrain. Latest SPC mesoanalysis does shows a slight 
straighting of the hodograph, which is supportive of both left and
right moving supercells, producing large hail, while still 
maintaining a tornado threat. There is a Tornado Watch in effect 
for Coconino, Navajo, and Yavapai counties through 6 PM MST. This 
is expected to a slight decline in extent for a couple hours after
6 PM as conditions become slightly unfavorable, however the 
overall environment will continued to support thunderstorms 
overnight with severe weather still a possibility. Severe 
thunderstorms bringing 1-2 inch hail have remained the primary 
threat thus far, with an isolated tornado risk. A secondary threat
of flash flooding is also in play given the deep moisture. 
However, fast storm motion with localized heavy rainfall rates in
thunderstorms will help to limit the areal coverage of flash 
flooding. Greatest risk for flash flooding will be sensitive burn
scars, washes, and areas susceptible to water running off onto 
roads and nearby property.

Thursday and Thursday evening...Threats of flash flooding and 
severe thunderstorms continue through the period, though the main
area is expected to shift more towards eastern Arizona as the
strong upper-level low moves over Arizona and then starts to push
off to the east Thursday evening. For flooding, we will remain in
a continuous fetch of deep tropical/subtropical moisture with 
modest instability and enhanced low-level flow. Precipitable Water
(a measure of atmospheric moisture) will rise to 0.8-1.2 inches 
across most of our area. This is highly anomalous for mid- 
October. Despite the fast expected storm motion, periods of 
training or back-building storms are possible and could lead to 
locally heavy rainfall rates with flash flooding concerns. Also 
several rounds of heavy rain are expected for most, and longer 
duration flooding of rivers, streams, normally dry washes, 
drainage basins, etc is possible. This is exacerbated further by 
very saturated surface conditions for all of northern AZ. As a 
result, a Flood Watch continues through 11 PM MST Thursday. The 
threat of flooding ends on Thursday evening as a cold front sweeps
from west to east and brings much drier air in its wake.

For the severe threat on Thursday, it is expected to shift a bit 
further east towards the Eastern Mogollon Rim and White Mountains 
with potential for strong storms along the propagating cold front.
SPC for Thursday as a Marginal risk (level 1 out of 5) for most of
northern AZ, with a small Slight risk (level 2 out of 5) for
portions of Gila and far southern Navajo and Apache counties. The
500 mb jet is expected start weakening Thursday afternoon and 
instability may be more limited for Thursday, though breaks in 
the clouds would increase instability due to daytime heating. 
Continue to monitor the weather and for any updated information.

Be prepared and have a way to receive warnings!

Friday and onward...Activity is expected to trend downward by Friday 
into the weekend after the main trough axis pushes past Northern AZ 
and drier air moves in. A closed low may linger across western AZ, 
and slight chances for showers and thunderstorms remain in the 
forecast each day. Expect lighter winds and temperatures remaining 
below normal otherwise.
